Goal: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from the limitation group 'Leakage-free generalisation protocol': L1, L2, L11, L20, L22, L27, L37, C2): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and with a simple supervised baseline trained on the same labelled images (L31) where relevant.

TITLE: Position-wise support normalisation of MVFA's branches
SUMMARY: Normalise each branch's patch score by the leave-one-out support scores at the same grid position, shrunk towards the global support statistic, so anatomy-driven offsets are removed without test-set statistics.
HYPOTHESIS: On spatially aligned modalities (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, OCT17), position-wise normalisation improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over global support percentiles at K >= 4, and it is not worse than global percentiles on ChestXray and HIS by more than 0.5 points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normaliser (test-set min-max; global support percentiles; position-wise support normalisation). For branch b, level l and position j: mu_j, sd_j from the K LOO support scores at j (and its 3x3 neighbourhood), shrunk: mu*_j = (n mu_j + 20 mu_g)/(n + 20), likewise sd; z = (s_j - mu*_j)/sd*_j, mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, false-positive rate in normal images per position (heat map), per-image score shift.
RATIONALE: Medical images of one modality are roughly aligned, and ADAN shows that much of an adapted CLIP map reflects anatomy. A single global normaliser per branch therefore mixes positions where normal anatomy scores high (e.g., skull, retinal layers) with positions where it scores low. Normalising each grid position by the support-normal scores at that position (shrunk towards the global statistic because K is small) removes anatomy-driven offsets inductively, before the unchanged 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: positional_refs(support_maps) computes per-position LOO statistics with a 3x3 neighbourhood and shrinkage weight 20. 2) test_few.py: per-image positional z-scores per branch and level, logistic map, 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: neighbourhood 3x3, shrinkage 20 (ablation {5, 20, 80}); no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, positional false-positive maps, score shift. Ablations: shrinkage; neighbourhood size. Falsified if no pixel-AUROC gain on aligned modalities.

TITLE: Anchor-geometry normalisation of MVFA's zero-shot branch
SUMMARY: Replace the softmax output of the zero-shot branch by the patch projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, standardise both branches with support LOO statistics, and fuse them with MVFA's unchanged rule.
HYPOTHESIS: Standardising the unit-direction projection makes the support-derived threshold transfer across held-out modalities with a realised-specificity spread at least 5 points smaller than with percentile-normalised softmax scores, at equal AUROC (within 1 point).
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: zero-shot branch representation and normaliser (test-set min-max on softmax; support percentiles on softmax; support standardisation of the unit-direction projection). For level l: u_l = (T_abn - T_nor)/||T_abn - T_nor||; zero-shot score s = <f_j/||f_j||, u_l>; z = (s - median_supp)/MAD_supp; few-shot branch standardised the same way; both mapped by a logistic to [0, 1]. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, and stability of the operating threshold across held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: MVFA's zero-shot branch is a two-way softmax over text anchors, so by Do Words Matter? its scale is fixed by the length of the anchor difference times the feature norm, a quantity that is constant per level and known without any test image. The two branches can then be put on a common scale analytically: express the zero-shot branch as the projection on the unit anchor-difference direction, and standardise it and the few-shot branch with support LOO statistics on that projection. This replaces test-set min-max with a geometry-derived, inductive normaliser and keeps 0.5 fusion and max pooling.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: anchor_direction(text_features) per level. 2) test_few.py: zero-shot map = projection on u_l; support LOO median and MAD per branch and level; logistic map; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: none; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std; fusion weight 0.5 and max pooling unchanged in every variant. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max) and the percentile normaliser of the problem statement (1st/99th percentiles of leave-one-out support patch scores). Motivating measurement for all variants: AUROC spread of the transductive pipeline over random half-size test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, spread of realised specificity across held-out datasets. Falsified if the threshold spread is not reduced.
